name: Queue manager
purpose: Own queue infrastructure: declaration, connection lifecycle, retry and dead-letter policy, and the enqueue API.
responsibilities: Declare queues, topics and dead-letter destinations
Own connection lifecycle, pooling and reconnection
Define retry counts, backoff strategy and dead-letter thresholds in one place
Expose a typed enqueue API to the rest of the system
Instrument queue depth, consumer lag and dead-letter volume
restrictions: Must NOT import consumers or job handlers
Must NOT hide delivery semantics callers need to reason about — at-least-once must stay visible in the API surface
Must NOT declare infrastructure as a side effect of the first enqueue; declaration is explicit and startup-time

deadLetterPolicy.description: Every queue has a dead-letter destination and a finite retry count. A queue without one turns a poison message into an infinite retry loop, which looks like load rather than a failure.

singleSourceOfPolicy.description: Retry, backoff and DLQ thresholds live here and nowhere else. A consumer or handler that implements its own retry defeats the broker's accounting and hides failures from queue metrics.

agentHints: Declaring infrastructure is a startup step, not a lazy side effect — make it explicit and idempotent.
Enqueue APIs should be typed per job, not a generic send(name, payload).
If you find yourself adding a retry loop outside this layer, the policy here is wrong instead.
Queue depth without consumer lag is a misleading metric; instrument both.
